subject: Probe pack exchange: custodianship, MAP milestones & rollback checklist
messages:
From: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: k.i@redwood.ai; legal@acme.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Probe pack exchange: scope, usage restrictions and timing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers look good. We discussed exchanging an assessment pack (prompt set + ~2k labeled test cases) so our ML team can run a small-calibration evaluation against Redwood Dedicated. Before we move data, two quick asks from our side so we can get procurement and infosec aligned:

- MAP: can you share a proposed mutual action plan with milestone dates for asset delivery, acceptance, and takedown?
- Usage limits: we need an explicit ephemeral-access lane (sandbox) and a hard destruction window (no copies retained beyond the takedown date).
- Proofs: Acme wants a simple verification artifact (SHA256 manifest) for delivered files and a brief audit log of who retrieved artifacts.
- License: trial-only, non-commercial evaluation; retention/derivative-use restrictions.

If you can send a draft MAP and acceptable timelines, I'll route to our infosec and legal. We aim to begin the run the week of Nov 22 if possible.

Thanks,
Ryan
Ryan Cole
Head of ML Ops, Acme AI

---

On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 14:07 Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@acme.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Probe pack exchange: scope, usage restrictions and timing

Ryan — great to hear you're ready to move forward. Attached is a compact MAP + checklist that captures our standard flow and the rollback items you asked about. I've attached: MAP_Timeline_Rollback_Checklist_v1.pdf (walks through deliverable dates and the takedown protocol) and probe_promptpack_v3.zip (encrypted tarball of prompts and the testcases summary).

High-level summary of the MAP we propose:

1) Asset delivery (Nov 17): Redwood uploads encrypted probe bundle to Acme-approved GCS bucket; we provide SHA256 manifest and per-file hash list.
2) Ephemeral sandbox (Nov 18–Dec 18): Acme will have time-boxed access to an ephemeral sandbox environment (no outbound network egress) provisioned in your account or a mutually-controlled ephemeral lane.
3) Acceptance gate (Dec 18): mutual acceptance step — both parties sign-off on subset sanity checks (smoke tests). If acceptance fails, auto-rollback and destruction within 48 hours per the MAP.
4) Takedown (Dec 21): destructive wipe of all copies; Redwood provides destruction proofs and access logs.

Key constraints we need from you now:
- Confirm legal text in section 4.2 (trial-only evaluation license). If Acme proposes edits, send redlines.
- Provide names and email addresses of infosec reviewers so we can configure access control.
- Are you ok with the proposed sandbox size (50GB) and a max of 10 concurrent inference sessions? If not, propose numbers.

Notes on custody & proofs: we produce an access log (user+timestamp+action) and a signed SHA256 manifest for the bundle. We do not retain a copy beyond the takedown window. We also offer ephemeral API credentials scoped to the sandbox.

Attachments:
- MAP_Timeline_Rollback_Checklist_v1.pdf (see section on "destruction proofs")
- probe_promptpack_v3.zip (encrypted; passphrase to be shared over OOB)

Next steps: please loop in your procurement contact and legal; if the above is a blocker, flag specific clauses and we'll try to accommodate. Proposed mutual acceptance cadence below — happy to shift.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Nov 13, 2026 at 09:34 Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@acme.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Probe pack exchange: scope, usage restrictions and timing

Ryan — quick technical clarifications from infra: 
- The sandbox will run on a dedicated VPC with no egress; inference SLO we can guarantee for the run is p95 <= 220ms for sequences <= 512 tokens on our dedicated profile.
- We plan to provide an audit log export in CSV (timestamp,user,email,action,object) and a signed JSON manifest (we include file hashes and a signature header).
- For the run: we support FP16 and int8-quantized models; please confirm whether your evaluation requires token-level logs (we avoid storing token-level outputs by default).

If Acme needs token-level output retention for model debugging, we'll need an explicit opt-in in the MAP and a short-addendum on retention and access controls.

Thanks,
Karthik
SVP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
